issues.description: Command names registered as quickmarks_reload/bookmarks_reload but tests/docs use hyphenated names
issues.detail: The methods are defined as `quickmarks_reload` and `bookmarks_reload`, which qutebrowser's cmdutils typically registers using underscores unless explicitly named. The feature tests invoke `:bookmarks-reload` and `:quickmarks-reload` (hyphenated). Existing similar commands use singular form (`quickmark-save`, `bookmark-add`); the inconsistent pluralization and the registered-vs-invoked name mismatch will cause command-not-found failures.

issues.description: Inconsistent naming with existing quickmark-*/bookmark-* command family
issues.detail: All other related commands are singular: `quickmark-add`, `quickmark-save`, `quickmark-del`, `bookmark-add`, `bookmark-del`, `bookmark-list`. Introducing plural `quickmarks-reload`/`bookmarks-reload` breaks the established command vocabulary and tab-completion grouping. Should be `quickmark-reload` and `bookmark-reload` for consistency.

issues.description: reload() re-initializes lineparser instead of re-reading existing one
issues.detail: `reload()` calls `self._init_lineparser()` which constructs a fresh LineParser each time. If save-manager or other components hold references to the original lineparser, they may now point to a stale object, causing later saves to write to a detached parser. Safer to call a read/refresh method on the existing `self._lineparser`.

issues.description: Reload silently discards unsaved in-memory changes without warning
issues.detail: `reload()` clears `self.marks` and reads from disk, dropping any quickmarks/bookmarks added since the last save. If the save-manager has pending writes queued, reload could race with them or undo the user's recent additions silently. Consider warning the user or forcing a save-then-reload sequence.

issues.description: Feature test scenarios are missing descriptive names
issues.detail: The two new scenarios in `urlmarks.feature` use bare `Scenario:` with no title, breaking the convention of every other scenario in the file (e.g., `Scenario: Saving a quickmark`). This hurts readability of test reports and is inconsistent with the surrounding file.

issues.description: Unit test doesn't verify clear-then-repopulate semantics or empty-file behavior
issues.detail: `test_reload` only covers the replace-one-entry case. It does not test that entries removed from disk are dropped (the clear() behavior), nor reload from an empty file, nor that a second `changed` signal fires. Given reload() now does the constructor's work, a wider coverage would catch regressions in `_init_lineparser` reuse.

review.summary: The PR adds reload commands for bookmarks and quickmarks by extracting the load logic into a reusable `reload()` method. The main concern is a likely command-name mismatch: the Python methods are `quickmarks_reload`/`bookmarks_reload` (plural) while the tests invoke `:quickmarks-reload`/`:bookmarks-reload`, and existing commands in the family use the singular `quickmark-*`/`bookmark-*` form — this will both break the tests and pollute the command vocabulary. Secondary concerns: `reload()` recreates the lineparser (potentially stranding references held elsewhere), unsaved in-memory changes are dropped silently, and the feature scenarios lack titles. Unit coverage is thin — only the replace case is exercised.
